correctness.rationale: The finite universe comprises exactly 27 labelled points and 117 three-point affine lines. Recursive cap generation and an independent exhaustive scan of all C(27,9)=4,686,825 subsets produce exactly 2,106 nine-caps; no cap extends to ten, proving maximality. One implementation compares all cap-pair intersections, the other generates literal three-point replacements. Both find 75,816 edges and degree 72 for every cap, and independently BFS from all 2,106 vertices with identical joint intersection/distance distributions. This establishes connectedness, both radius and diameter four, and that all distance-four pairs are disjoint. Source Proposition 2.2 establishes the interpretation of their unique three-cap partition; no infinite inference or undocumented computation is required.

value.rationale: For the smallest genuinely three-dimensional ternary cap problem, a natural local-search question is how many optimal points must be replaced simultaneously and how far extremizers are in the resulting graph. Here exchanges of one or two are impossible, three exchanges yield a connected 72-regular 2,106-state graph, and the exact distance-four antipodes are the disjoint partners from the classical cap partition. The 24 three-point-overlap caps at distance three and the unavoidable fourth step between disjoint caps give nontrivial, geometrically interpretable shortest-path detours. These are not routine restatements of the previously known maximum cardinality, cap equivalence or partition uniqueness.
